title: How to chase a late invoice without losing the client
excerpt: Three emails, three tones, and when to pick up the phone. The sequence that gets most invoices paid within a week.
content:
Most late invoices aren't a sign of a bad client. They're a sign of a busy one. Here's the order that works.

Day 3: assume it slipped

A short, friendly note with the invoice attached and the Pay button. No apology, no blame.

Day 7: be clear

Say the amount, the due date and the number of days late. Ask when you can expect payment.

Day 14: be firm, then call

Mention your late fee if your terms have one. If there's still nothing, a phone call usually settles it in a minute.

Reminders can send the first three for you.

title: When and how to raise your rates
excerpt: If you're booked solid, you're too cheap. How to tell clients, how much to add, and what to do if someone says no.
content:
Most freelancers raise their rates too late and too little. Here's a simple way to do it.

Raise for new clients first

Quote new clients your new rate. Nothing to explain, and you'll see quickly if it holds.

Give existing clients notice

Two months' notice, one short email, the new rate and the date. Most won't blink.

Add 10 to 20 percent

Enough to matter, small enough that good clients stay.

Change your rate once in Tally and every new invoice uses it.

title: How much should a freelancer set aside for tax?
excerpt: A rule of thumb for each country we support, and why a separate account makes April painless.
content:
The short answer: more than you think, and every time you're paid.

A rule of thumb

Put aside 25 to 30 percent of every payment until you know your real figure. Your accountant can tell you the right number after one year.

Use a separate account

Money you can't see is money you don't spend. Move the set-aside amount the day you're paid.

Check every quarter

Compare what you've saved with what you'll owe, and top up if you're behind.

Tax set aside shows the figure on every payment.

title: Five habits of freelancers who get paid on time
excerpt: Clear terms, deposits and invoices sent the day the work is done. Small habits that add up to weeks sooner.
content:
We looked at 40,000 invoices. The freelancers paid fastest have five things in common.

1. Terms agreed before work starts

Payment terms in the proposal, not a surprise on the invoice.

2. Deposits on new clients

A deposit filters out clients who won't pay and pays for the first week.

3. Invoices sent the same day

Invoices sent the day the work is delivered are paid nine days sooner on average.

4. Easy ways to pay

A Pay button gets paid twice as fast as bank details at the bottom of a PDF.

5. Reminders on

Polite, automatic and in your words. Start free and turn them on.
